question: Should OpenClaw accept a generic durable allow-always plugin approval API and core SQLite trust store, and what non-sensitive owner/scope contract must built-in Skill Workshop use if it opts in?
rationale: This changes a plugin-facing API and a durable approval security boundary; the code can be repaired mechanically only after maintainers decide the accepted trust model and built-in owner contract.

options.title: Fix and accept the durable API
options.body: Keep the generic API, but require a stable core/plugin owner, non-sensitive scope key, second-call reuse coverage, and docs that match the final contract before merge.

options.title: Split Skill Workshop out
options.body: Land only the generic persistence mechanism after API review and keep Skill Workshop on allow-once/deny until its owner, audit, and scope model are separately approved.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or pause this PR if durable plugin approvals are not part of the desired plugin trust model right now.

recommendation.title: Fix and accept the durable API
recommendation.body: Keep the generic API, but require a stable core/plugin owner, non-sensitive scope key, second-call reuse coverage, and docs that match the final contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent adjacent merged work touched the same Skill Workshop approval, protocol, and plugin approval surfaces, making this the best available owner for the API/security direction decision.
